result.title: Spatiotemporal Reconstruction of Auroral Precipitations with Neural Fields
result.comment: Accepted to the IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV 2027). Camera-ready version with supplementary material. 17 pages, 15 figures
result.summary: Auroras provide remote optical observations of energetic electrons precipitating into the upper atmosphere, and whose energy distribution encodes key information about large scale magnetospheric processes. Recovering the underlying electron precipitation field from ground-based camera images of auroras remains a challenging inverse problem. Existing auroral tomography techniques are often limited to simplified static settings, discrete spatial and energy grids, or strong assumptions on the electron energy spectrum. We propose to model the dynamic auroral electron precipitation field via a temporally conditioned neural network. The state of the precipitation field at each frame is represented by a per-frame latent code driven by learned discrete dynamics. A shared decoder maps horizontal positions and latent states to electron energy spectra. The predicted flux is converted to multi-wavelength volume emission rates and rendered into camera images accounting for delayed emissions. We evaluate the method on synthetic dynamic auroral sequences and real multi-view auroral videos, showing that the proposed representation produces temporally coherent precipitation reconstructions and image projections consistent with the observations.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把极光电子沉降场建模为时间条件神经场：每帧状态压缩为一个 latent code，由学习到的离散动力学在帧间演化，共享解码器将水平位置与 latent 映射为能谱，再经多波长辐射与延迟效应渲染成相机图像，在合成动态序列与真实多视角视频上验证重建的时间一致性与投影一致性。
AI.relevance_reason: 「逐帧 latent code + 离散状态转移 + 可微前向渲染反演」的结构可供核查是否能类比 LVR 中 latent 推理状态的更新与由观测反推状态的监督，但研究对象是极光层析物理反演，与 VLM 推理无直接联系，迁移性需较多判断。
